market.summary: Little has changed since Friday. The KLCI closed 1.6 points lower at 1,670.02 in a quiet session (RM2.40bn traded, down from RM2.69bn), and it is still below its 10-month moving average, so your rule that the monthly trend must be up still fails. The index is sitting near the bottom of its 3-month range (1,655–1,753) and foreign funds sold a net RM473m last week. The one new thing is oil: Brent is back above US$106 after Washington rejected Iran's offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which lifts refiners and raises costs for everyone else. Keep waiting for a close back above about 1,701 (the 10-month MA) before buying.

sources.title: Bursa Malaysia Ends Marginally Lower Amid Lack Of Fresh Catalysts

notes: Run on Mon 28 Sep, 9.30pm, after the close. The screen covered all 1,134 Bursa stocks (265 liquid: market cap RM300m+ and RM500k+ average daily trading value), looking for bases near highs, quiet buying and breakouts on double volume, and excluding anything overheated (RSI above 75, more than 25% above its 50-day MA, or up more than 25% in a week). Three things changed since Friday. (1) A new name, Binastra, broke out to a record high on 2.1× volume and is the first candidate in weeks that passes your P/E limit of 20 as well as the ROE and debt tests. (2) Oil is the new macro driver — Brent above US$106 — but the move is confined to refiners, with no follow-through in oil services, so it is a sector note rather than a buy list. (3) Budget 2027 now has a firm date: Friday 9 October. Follow-ups on Friday's six: Gamuda is still 1.8% under its RM5.00 trigger but volume has dried up to 0.6× normal; Southern Cable gave back 4.2% today on 2.1× volume after last week's 11% jump, so the base at RM2.91 is intact but that down-day on heavy volume is a warning; UMS Integration keeps its place but is demoted, because 10-day volume fell from 3.0× to 0.2× normal and the quiet-buying case was the whole reason it was there; Kelington (−3.0% on no volume), SunCon (still under its 50-day MA) and Mega First are dropped — Mega First fell 2.6% on 3.1× volume and lost the 200-day MA it had only just reclaimed, which is a failed reclaim rather than a base. Nothing is buyable while the market check fails. On your P/E limit: Binastra shows the limit is less of a problem than it looked on Friday — a 16.5× stock with 47% ROE and 61% earnings growth does exist inside these themes — so leave it at 20 and treat P/E 20–30 names as exceptions that need a specific reason.

catalysts.title: Budget 2027 tabled on 9 October
catalysts.detail: The date is now fixed: the Prime Minister tables Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat on Friday 9 October. Energy transition, data centres, infrastructure allocations and any change to electricity tariffs or fuel subsidies are the usual market movers. Treat it as an event risk in both directions — stocks in the favoured themes often run up in the week before and sell off on the day itself.

catalysts.title: Oil above US$100 and the Strait of Hormuz
catalysts.detail: Brent traded above US$106 on Monday after President Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and Saudi Arabia intercepted drones heading for Riyadh. For Bursa this cuts both ways: refiners and oil producers earn more and government oil revenue rises, but fuel and freight costs squeeze everyone else, and high oil has already been blamed for pushing the KLCI lower this month. Any credible de-escalation would reverse the refining trade fast.
